A user-interface component sheet for a fantasy grand-strategy game, laid out cleanly on a flat neutral dark background with generous spacing, viewed flat and front-on, like a designer's style board: (1) top left, one complete framed window panel with a title band, a close button in its corner and an empty body; (2) top right, one horizontal row of the same rectangular button shown in five states left to right: normal, hover, pressed, disabled, selected; each button carries a short label in plain English (Normal, Hover, Pressed, Disabled, Selected); (3) middle left, a tooltip box with a heading line and two short lines of plain text; (4) middle right, a row of four icon frames: an empty frame, a frame holding a small painted emblem of a horse head, one holding a sheaf of wheat, one holding a tower, all four frames identical in shape and size; (5) bottom left, a horizontal divider ornament and a tab strip of three tabs, the middle tab selected; (6) bottom right, a progress meter half full and a small checkbox on and off. Every component clearly belongs to one consistent family of materials, borders and colours. No logo, no watermark, no signature, no crosses, no real-world religious or national symbols. Visual direction "The Banner Hall": the interface is made of the same craft as the realms' embroidered banners shown in the reference image (flat cut-cloth appliqué and embroidery on a deep dyed field with a cultural hem). Panels are heavy dark dyed wool cloth with a fine visible weave, stretched taut, edged by an embroidered hem of a simple repeating stitched pattern and a couched gold cord; title bands are a strip of contrasting cloth stitched on; buttons are padded cloth tabs with stitched edges and small brass grommets, hover shows brighter thread, pressed sinks, disabled is plain undyed linen, selected gets a gold-thread border; icons are bold flat appliqué emblems with few colours inside identical round stitched cloth roundels; dividers are a braided cord; the tooltip is a sewn cloth label. Palette of natural dyes: deep madder red, woad blue, weld yellow, walnut brown, undyed linen cream, with gold thread as the single accent. Bold, simple, hand-made, readable, no painted shading on emblems, no fine illustration on the chrome. The reference image is one of this world's realm banners; the small horse-head emblem in the icon frame should be in the same craft.

prompt: Painted dark-fantasy strategy-game interface art, crisp and clean, high detail, flat even lighting. No modern objects (no gears, no rifles, no tanks, no telephones), no crosses, no real-world religious or national symbols, no sun discs, no demons or skulls in the chrome, no figures or faces in the chrome. A full-screen mock-up of the in-game interface of a fantasy grand-strategy game in the style of Hearts of Iron, landscape 16:9 screen layout, shown exactly as the player sees the monitor, front-on, no device frame. Visual direction "The Chronicle": the interface reads like the Chronicle of Aoaz, a great illuminated record kept in a stone hall. Window frames are carved blue-grey slate with a crisp bevelled edge and a thin inlaid bronze line; reading panels are pale vellum with dark ink text and small rubricated red initials at the start of titles; icons are engraved ink seals, monochrome dark-ink line drawings of one consistent line weight inside identical circular seal frames, with a single touch of rubric red or gold leaf; buttons are flat stone plaques with an inlaid bronze rim, hover lightens the stone, pressed shows a deeper bevel, disabled is dull unpolished stone, selected gets a gold-leaf rim; dividers are a ruled double ink line with a small knotwork centre. Palette: slate blue-grey, vellum cream, iron-gall ink, rubric red, gold leaf, with verdigris and amber for status. Crisp, scholarly, very high contrast and readability, quiet ornament. The screen shows, together and all at once: (1) across the very top, a slim resource top bar with a realm banner flag at the far left, small resource icons with short numbers, and a date plate at the far right; (2) directly beneath its left half, a narrower second strip, the "Aoaz bar", holding a "Realm" button, an age plate reading "4A 1748", a small dark-gathering meter with a value of 10, three small country meters with tiny icons, and one small round sigil button; (3) a large open national focus tree panel filling the left and centre of the screen: a titled window with a grid of about fourteen focus nodes (each a small square painted icon above a short title plate) joined by clean connector lines, one node highlighted as in progress with a thin progress bar, and a description panel at the bottom; (4) an event window on the right side, overlapping the map: a title, a painted landscape picture of a walled riverside town at dusk in a frame, three short paragraphs of body text, and two option buttons stacked beneath. Behind everything, a painted campaign map of a fantasy continent with coasts, rivers, forests and coloured realm borders is visible at the edges. Interface text is short, plain and legible English; there is no logo, no watermark and no signature. The interface is one consistent visual system: the same panel material, the same border, the same button shape and the same icon frame everywhere. The first reference image is one of this world's realm banners (use it as the realm flag in the top bar and as the craft and style reference for emblems); the second reference image shows this world's painted portrait style (do not show a portrait in this screen).
